rooms.question: Can random positions still refuse to be neighbours?
rooms.ontology: A sample distribution specifies how positions are selected; an exclusion radius constrains relations among accepted samples.
rooms.action: Observe the point cloud from two sides; find the closest visible pair before moving any pickable point.
rooms.observable: The original cloud avoids pairs closer than 0.25 local units. Moving a point later need not preserve the generation rule.
rooms.mechanism: spawn_points defaults BLUE_NOISE; _generate_blue_noise rejects candidates within minimum distance and caps100 attempts per requested point.
rooms.limit: A constrained sample is not proof that all randomness is evenly spaced. Perspective conceals depth and later manipulation changes the sample.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Place matched uniform and blue-noise samples with the same requested count and volume, and reveal rejected candidates.

rooms.question: What remains recognisable while a column changes shape?
rooms.ontology: A surface can retain its construction and repeated profile while vertex positions and material values vary over time.
rooms.action: Watch one column through a cycle, then compare it with a neighbouring column at the same moment.
rooms.observable: Shafts bend and droop while rotation rates and melt phases differ across columns.
rooms.mechanism: Scene specifies13 columns,8-unit height,13-point layout; _process advances per-column rotation and sin(time*melt_speed+i), rebuilding spiral shaft mesh.
rooms.limit: This is programmed deformation, not a simulation of stone losing strength or an available noise-amplitude experiment. Periodic change does not establish physical erosion.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Add an intact reference column and a freeze/phase control so the visitor can separate deformation from rotation.

rooms.question: Is a restless surface changing its underlying shape or only how that shape is expressed?
rooms.ontology: A field assigns a scalar to a coordinate; a readout turns that scalar into displacement or colour on an existing mesh.
rooms.action: Watch a section of the ring, then move to see its opening and silhouette.
rooms.observable: The ring remains the support for changing displacement and hue, although large displacement can obscure its torus form.
rooms.mechanism: noiseTorus vertex samples interpolated value noise at object XZ plus timed offset and moves vertices along NORMAL; scene height_multiplier0.2 and noise_speed0.935.
rooms.limit: Spatial correlation does not mean the field remembers a visitor or keeps a neighbour list. A changing view also changes what the visitor can judge.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Make relief and colour-only plate versions share a frozen field so the same values support different readings.
rooms.cautions: Source read only; actual museum runtime, reachability, controls and learner understanding remain unverified. No visitor readout control; noiselayers remains secondary and is not required for this core.

rooms.question: Can you remove matter without changing the field that decides where it could appear?
rooms.ontology: A voxel is a discrete volume sample. A threshold classifies a sampled scalar as occupied or empty.
rooms.action: Move THRESH slowly while leaving SCALE and SEED alone; compare the small volume and linked voxel exhibit, then return THRESH to its earlier position.
rooms.observable: Higher thresholds retain fewer samples; the connected display also rebuilds. Returning the threshold with the seed fixed restores the same classification.
rooms.mechanism: Sculptor samples Perlin fBm with a height bias and compares n-height_bias>threshold; broadcasts threshold,normalised frequency,octaves,seed to voxelnoise_receivers. Receiver uses a simplex field, so the pair shares controls rather than identical geometry.
rooms.limit: The cut classifies a field chosen by the author. Occupied cubes are an encoding, not evidence that matter itself is binary. Linked images are not identical field copies.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Let visitors compare fixed threshold and changing seed, then fixed seed and changing threshold; preserve both results side by side.
rooms.cautions: Source read only; actual museum runtime, reachability, controls and learner understanding remain unverified. No octaves VR slider despite header comment. Group broadcast may reach receivers beyond this room in museum; runtime pairing must be checked.

rooms.question: What changes when the field surrounds you instead of sitting on a bench?
rooms.ontology: A shader evaluates a rule across a surface; several spatial frequencies can be summed before they become colour.
rooms.action: Pause at a visible wall, trace a broad patch and a smaller detail within it, then compare another face.
rooms.observable: Large cloudy regions carry smaller variation; the material changes with time, and differently timed surfaces need not match.
rooms.mechanism: WallNoiseShader sums6 octaves, halves amplitude and doubles frequency; noiseroom updates room time and wall time at0.7 of it, plus colour and density.
rooms.limit: Six superimposed scales are not six separate visible teaching strips. Motion and colour are coupled, so watching alone cannot isolate each parameter.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Offer a freeze control and single-octave comparison with equal framing and brightness.

sources.fact: noise2d dispatch and six-iteration octave sum.

rooms.question: Does placing noise on a sphere mean one noise is being fed into another?
rooms.ontology: A sampling domain is the coordinates at which a function is evaluated; the supporting mesh and the sampled function are different things.
rooms.action: Compare the sphere silhouette with the ring you encountered earlier; follow a patch across the curved surface.
rooms.observable: The same shader family deforms a different support, with finer spatial frequency and a larger enclosing form.
rooms.mechanism: Sphere uses noisePlanet2, the same value-noise interpolation and normal displacement family as noisetorus; scene readout defaults relief.
rooms.limit: The placed sphere does not implement domain warping. Curved noisy geometry alone cannot demonstrate noise used to displace sampling coordinates.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Add paired direct-sample and warped-sample surfaces with the same seed and visible coordinate displacement.

sources.fact: 37–59: direct XZ sampling plus timed translation, not nested noise.

rooms.cautions: Source read only; actual museum runtime, reachability, controls and learner understanding remain unverified. Map description promises domain warping that this primary does not perform. Record as a future experiment, not a solved teaching claim.

rooms.question: When a field becomes ground, which variations become a route?
rooms.ontology: A heightfield assigns one height to each planar position and turns samples into a mesh and collision surface.
rooms.action: Inspect the green terrain from its edge; follow a ridge with your eye and compare a gentle route with a steeper one.
rooms.observable: Neighbouring heights form a continuous-looking terrain with broad and small features, fixed after construction.
rooms.mechanism: NoiseSpace generate_space samples noise_2d over10×10 coordinates, multiplies by height_scale, creates mesh and collision.
rooms.limit: A heightfield cannot give two ground heights to the same XZ location; caves and overhangs need another representation. Ten-dimensional parameter-space controls are absent.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Author two adjacent terrain patches differing only in octave count, then let the visitor choose and explain a route.

rooms.question: What would make two noise surfaces a fair comparison?
rooms.ontology: A noise basis, seed, sampling frequency and visible encoding jointly determine a displayed field.
rooms.action: Compare neighbouring sample heights and colour changes in the two cube fields; identify what the display lets you see and what it leaves unnamed.
rooms.observable: Both surfaces are sampled cube fields. Different appearances alone do not establish different algorithms.
rooms.mechanism: Both placed tokens are bare. PerlinNoise generator defaults simplex and NoiseVisualizer chooses TYPE_SIMPLEX for that value; SimplexVisualizer also uses simplex.
rooms.limit: This room currently cannot support its titled Perlin-versus-Simplex conclusion: both defaults use simplex-family noise, with independent seeds and different sampling paths.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Set generator=perlin explicitly on one placement and fix matched seeds, dimensions and readout before asking visitors to attribute differences to the basis.

rooms.question: What can you carry out of a sequence when the busy demonstrations are gone?
rooms.ontology: A reference object supports recall and comparison; the explanation now has to be supplied by the visitor.
rooms.action: Pause beside the dark sphere and describe one earlier encounter in terms of field, sample and readout; then name a different outcome from changing the threshold rather than the seed.
rooms.observable: The sphere pulses and slowly rotates; it does not display a new noise field or a correctness verdict.
rooms.mechanism: dark_sphere _process varies emission and rotation sinusoidally; map places it with exit utility in the same central cell.
rooms.limit: A familiar marker cannot verify understanding. A remembered image may omit the parameter and representation that produced it.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Let visitors leave two competing explanations or route memories here, each naming an observation that would distinguish them.
